serviceDescription: This feature service presents geographic boundaries for transient and non-transient non-community water system service areas across the United States, supporting monitoring and management of public water systems.
description:
Overview

This feature service provides geographic data on service areas associated with transient and non-transient non-community water systems across the United States. It supports information about the boundaries and characteristics of water supply coverage for these systems, which are critical for ensuring safe and reliable drinking water in facilities such as schools, daycare centers, places of work, gas stations, hotels, and other public water systems not serviced by a community water system.

Feature Layers

  • NCWS Service Areas: This polygon layer represents the spatial boundaries of service areas served by transient and non-transient non-community water systems. It includes data fields covering system identifiers, population served, type of water system, source of water, and service connections. The layer also contains details on the area and perimeter of these service boundaries, enabling analysis of service coverage and geographic distribution.
  • NCWS Serivce Area Points: Service areas described by the mean center location of the public water system

Geographic Coverage

The data covers service areas and points for transient and non-transient non-community water systems throughout the United States, extending from the continental US to all territories with the exception of Guam. Latitude and longitude ranges spanning roughly from -166.6 to 145.8 degrees longitude and 13.5 to 70.4 degrees latitude.

Sources and Data Integrity

The data is managed and provided by the Environmental Protection Agency's Office of Water, with detailed facility reports and data sources referenced in the attribute information. This ensures authoritative and up-to-date information relevant to public water system management and regulatory oversight.

Use Cases

  • Supporting regulatory agencies in monitoring and managing transient and non-transient non-community water systems.
  • Assisting public health professionals in identifying water system coverage and assessing potential risks in schools, daycare centers, and other facilities.
  • Providing planners and water utilities with spatial insights into service connections, population served, and system typologies for infrastructure development and resource allocation.
  • Connects Safe Drinking Water Act health-based violations to potential consumers of these violations.

Public Water System Definitions

EPA defines three types of public water systems. This dataset contains two of the three: Transient and Non-Transient Non-Community Water Systems. 

  • Non-Transient Non-Community Water System (NTNCWS): A public water system that regularly supplies water to at least 25 of the same people at least six months per year. Some examples are schools, factories, office buildings, and hospitals which have their own water systems.

  • Transient Non-Community Water System (TNCWS): A public water system that provides water in a place such as a gas station or campground where people do not remain for long periods of time.

The third type are Community Water Systems. These service areas have also been published by EPA’s Office of Water and are defined by:

  • Community Water System (CWS): A public water system that supplies water to the same population year-round.
